Global Warming Activists Want to Make Food More Expensive

Making food across the board more expensive seems spectacularly retarded to me.

What I *could * imagine would be making meat more expensive. I'm no vegetarian and like me a good steak as much as the next guy, but meat consumption in the western world has skyrocketed since the 1950, without producing anything good other than continually increasing obesity and first world-diseases.

At the same time, meat may fetch better prices than vegetables or fruits, but also requires much larger agricultural areas to provide the same quantity of foodstuffs when compared to say, wheat. And let's not even get started on the questionable ethical aspects of modern cage system housing, the medical concerns that pop up if you're eating the meat of animals that are so pumped up on drugs and antibiotics that Woodstock looks like a teetotaller conventiony by comparison, etc, etc.

To emphasize: I do not call for a complete ban on meat. But if you approach a state where burgers, chicken nuggets, and hot dogs effectively become staple foods over bread, potatoes, peas, and carrots, you know something is amiss.
